purpose: Three conceptual studio 3D illustrations of modular sensing skin applied over RP1 robot limb shells

prompts.prompt:
Use case: product-mockup. Create the FIRST of a coherent three-image series demonstrating ROBOSKIN electronic skin installed ON TOP OF the RoboParty RP1 humanoid in the reference. The reference image is for robot identity and proportions only; do not reproduce its Chinese text or technical callouts.
A premium, convincing industrial studio 3D visualization, wide landscape composition, white/light-gray seamless studio, soft contact shadows, crisp realistic materials. Show two full-body views of the SAME recognizable RP1: a dominant front three-quarter view with one elbow gently bent, and a slightly smaller rear three-quarter view. Both robots fully in frame, feet visible, no human figures.
CRITICAL: visibly apply a new conformal sensory skin overlay to BOTH upper arms, BOTH forearms, BOTH thighs and BOTH shins; this must look installed over the existing robot shells, not a bare robot with painted patches. Preserve RP1's rounded white head, black face with two vertical eyes, white torso shell, blue shoulders, distinctive blue hip structure, proportions, hands and feet. Leave fingers, soles, head, joint bearing surfaces and ventilation clear.
Skin design: thin, soft, charcoal-gray replaceable sleeves/panels, smoothly following each individual rigid limb segment, with finely textured matte silicone protective outer surface, restrained teal perimeter seals, neat small seams and integrated flush retaining edges. Each upper/lower limb segment has its own separate panel; clean visible clearance gaps around elbow and knee joints. No bulky exoskeleton, no skin stretched over a joint, no armored plates, no exposed large circuit boards, no dangling wire bundles. Local small controller housings tucked into panel proximal edges; only a short subtle protected cable visible at one elbow. The sensory laminate is physically beneath the protective surface. Show one small tasteful local turquoise contact-response graphic on a forearm as a conceptual visualization, not an all-body heat map. Skin must occupy broad useful outer-limb areas and be unmistakable at thumbnail size. The blue and white RP1 parts remain clearly identifiable between covered zones.
Minimal typography: top left "ROBOSKIN"; beneath it exact Hebrew "עור חישה על זרועות ורגליים". Small bottom corner exact Hebrew "הדמיית תכנון". No other text or claims, no numeric specs, no logos other than ROBOSKIN, no Chinese, no watermark. High-detail polished engineering presentation, attractive but credible, approximately 16:9 landscape.

Use case: scientific-educational. Image TWO in the ROBOSKIN installed robot-skin series.
Reference 1 is the APPROVED visual identity: the exact white-and-blue RP1 humanoid with charcoal soft sensory panels and fine teal edges. Reference 2 is original RP1 geometry. Create a polished landscape studio 3D engineering illustration explaining how thin skin is mounted over this humanoid's LIMBS. Preserve recognizable RP1 proportions, head and existing shell, materials and visual language from reference1. No Chinese, no original callout sheet.
Composition: left third contains the whole RP1 robot wearing the same dark conformal segmented skin on arms and legs, one arm gently raised to reveal a forearm. A restrained zoom connector leads from that forearm to a large, beautifully rendered exploded cutaway in the right two-thirds. The cutaway is a curved forearm shell with a removable thin skin cassette directly above it; clearly the skin is mounted OUTSIDE the existing white robot shell. Keep fingers incidental, not the subject.
Outside-to-inside layer order, visually clear and physically plausible:
1. Outermost flexible protective TPU wear film, matte charcoal with teal perimeter rim, a corner gently peeled up; no exposed sensor on the outside.
2. Immediately under that cover, exactly TWO tiny near-surface temperature sensor islands on a slim amber flexible strip located at an edge away from pressure electrodes. These are isolated point sensors, not a full thermal-imaging layer.
3. Thin separated carbon resistive sensing islands over a perforated spacer and interdigitated gold electrode pairs on a flexible amber substrate; recognizable orderly rectangular sensor array, no thick individual silicone buttons. Separate layers with modest exploded spacing for illustration. Printed tracks remain on this local panel.
4. Thin electrically insulating curved removable carrier, supported by the white robot forearm shell. No drilling through structural robot parts.
A compact covered local controller at the proximal panel edge connects with a short reinforced flex tail, and only one slender protected four-conductor power/data cable leaves it. No wires crossing through the sensing surface. No fake schematic or numeric performance claim.
Five readable Hebrew callouts with precise thin leader lines: "שכבת הגנה ניתנת להחלפה" points to protective outer film; "שתי נקודות טמפרטורה" points to the two tiny islands; "שכבת מגע ולחץ יחסי" points to resistive sensing laminate; "תושבת מבודדת" points to insulating carrier; "בקר מקומי" points to compact controller.
Title "ROBOSKIN" and subtitle "מה נמצא מתחת לעור". Footer exact Hebrew "הדמיית תכנון · עובי השכבות מוגדל להמחשה".
Soft white studio, high-quality realistic materials, sharp detail, sensible clean whitespace, refined industrial design, 16:9 landscape. Image not CAD manufacturing instructions. Skin clearly visible on robot and exploded arm, no resemblance to human flesh, no added organs.

Use case: product-mockup / scientific-educational. Image THREE in the ROBOSKIN skin-on-RP1 series. Reference1 is approved skin styling and robot identity; reference2 gives original RP1 geometry. Make a premium wide studio 3D visualization of removable sensory skin on MOVING HUMANOID LIMBS, showing an elbow and a knee, not fingers.
Same recognizable white-and-blue RP1 hardware, same thin charcoal-gray soft matte skin cassettes with restrained teal edge seals as reference1. Skin is fitted over the white shells on individual rigid limb segments. Not armor, no thick padding, no carbon-fiber mechanical exoskeleton.
Composition is a clear diptych on a white seamless backdrop:
LEFT: a large close three-quarter view of the robot's arm from blue shoulder through upper arm and forearm, elbow moderately bent. Both rigid segments wear separate conformal skin panels; the WHITE mechanical elbow and its motion gap stay exposed. A single slender black jacketed power/data cable makes a generous smooth service loop near the joint rotation axis, with a clamp on each rigid segment. It must not be pinched in the elbow crease, and no PET sensor laminate stretches over the articulation. The skin rests flush against the shell, with modest visible thickness at edges.
RIGHT: the same robot's thigh and shin, knee moderately bent, skin panels clearly installed above and below the knee with a visible clearance gap. Show a forearm-sized example of a removable curved skin cassette near the lower right, slightly lifted from its matching carrier on the shin with two discreet fasteners at the non-sensing edge and a short flex tail leading to a covered controller. This illustrates replacement, not skin tearing or a floating unrelated board. The sensor grid can be subtly visible on the underside of the lifted cassette, while installed outer surfaces remain fully protected. Expose enough blue hip and white knee hardware to identify RP1.
Minimal annotation: title "ROBOSKIN"; subtitle "תנועה חופשית והחלפה פשוטה". Three precise Hebrew callouts only: "מרווח לתנועה" points to exposed elbow/knee gap; "כבל תקשורת והזנה" points to the protected service-loop cable; "פאנל ניתן להחלפה" points to removable cassette.
Small footer "הדמיית תכנון · התאמה מכנית טרם אומתה".
No numeric angles, no certified clearance or durability claims, no heat map, no bare finger tactile sensor, no human skin, no Chinese or watermark. Consistent soft studio lighting, finely textured charcoal protection, crisp realistic geometry, landscape 16:9.
